decisions: *Base:* `onia_loop` from `main` (frozen performance baseline `5c5b573794`); `onia_fks` is read for its constants and pole formulas only.

*Scheme:* MadLoop-native: 't Hooft–Veltman, 4-dimensional external projectors, Coulomb term dropped at $v = 0$ (part of the LDME), on-shell $m_Q$ and $Z_2$, $overline("MS")$ $alpha_s$ with $n_l$ light flavours.
*Timing:* on this host, paired alternating runs; accepted when the upper 95% bound of candidate ÷ baseline is at most 1.05 for every benchmark process, results identical.

*TIRust:* extensions and the pin belong to the TIRust development session; none is made here (requests and reproducers in `research/`). The pin `6ba4b53` is its MadGraph7 PR \#557, taken onto `onia_loop` with the approval of TIRust's owner.
status_lines: *S-wave, one bound state* (singlet or octet, any $J$) with elementary particles: the analytic $2 -> 1$ and $e^+ e^-$ results reproduced to $10^(-8)$, the published precision or MadLoop's accuracy estimate (@analytic); $2 -> 2$ poles as predicted, finite parts confirmed by the $v -> 0$ extrapolation of ordinary integrals (@twotwo).

*TIRust in double precision*, stable points in every frame. The other libraries fail at threshold, not always detected by MadLoop's tests: their results are now reported unstable, and TIRust is the default chain (@reducers).

*TIRust pin `6ba4b53`* (since 2026-11-27, MadGraph7 PR \#557; before `1c130a81`, @pin6ba): it has PRs \#47, \#55, \#56 and \#58. Every point of @analytic and @tab:mg255 is stable on it, and the examples of @v16all give the same return codes as on da7902b.

*Two bound states* ($e^+ e^- -> J\/psi thin eta_c$): stable on the pin, Gong–Wang reproduced to its seven digits ($5 dot 10^(-8)$; $b$, $t$ excluded from the loops), bit-identical to 08cca00 and da7902b; the old pin refused lanes there (@analytic).

*QP rescue and threshold:* the old pin's binary128 path refused the threshold lanes, so such points were reported unstable, not wrong. The pin rescues them, and serves $g g -> J\/psi thin g$ just above threshold in double precision (280 points at 3.02–3.8 GeV; @pin6ba).

*P-wave, one bound state* (@pwave): with TIRust 48958d1 (its PRs now pinned) the $2 -> 1$ literature values reproduced to $10^(-12)$, the poles as predicted with the $P -> S$ term of the soft current, also for $u overline(u) -> chi_(c 0) g$ and $g u -> chi_(c 0) u$.

*An S-wave and a P-wave state* ($e^+ e^- -> J\/psi thin chi_(c J)$, @sp): with TIRust 08cca00 (its PRs now pinned) the poles vanish as predicted, and the angular average of the finite part reproduces the closed form of Wang, Ma and Chao to $10^(-7)$ in double precision and $10^(-15)$ in quadruple precision ($b$, $t$ excluded from the loops; as heavy quarks at 10–100 TeV they left a floor of $10^(-7)$, @tab:qpfloor).

*S-wave onium + jet against MG5 2.5.5* (@mg255): every point stable on the pin, within MadLoop's estimate of the reference ($b$, $t$ excluded from the loops): $4 dot 10^(-9)$ at the points the old pin served, up to $3.4 dot 10^(-7)$ at the near-threshold points it refused ($1.4 dot 10^(-8)$ on da7902b). With the $b$, $t$ at $10^4$ GeV, the earlier setup, the old pin was within $2.3 dot 10^(-6)$: their counterterm rounding.

*Stability profiles* (@stability, after appendix C of arXiv:1604.01363), charmonium and bottomonium: S waves steep, apart from points the old pin refused (3% at 1 TeV) and a tail of true double-precision errors in 1–2% of the $J\/psi$, $Upsilon$ points; the P-wave singlets lose digits in double precision at 1 TeV, not at 20 GeV, through TIRust's pentagons with a doubled line. TIRust 5025e12 (PR \#56) with the bridge patch for its relation tiers and a binary64 gate (MadGraph7\#528) fixes all three: no point of any process above $10^(-3)$, no S wave above $10^(-6)$, no rescue at 1 TeV, 18–49% more time for the P waves at 20 GeV (@stability). The P-wave octets $e^+ e^- -> Q overline(Q) thin [n^((8))] thin g$ stay below $10^(-4)$ even with 48958d1.

*80-bit switch for the P waves* (@ep): `#PWaveExtendedPrecision` (off by default) computes the double-precision passes in extended precision. At 1 TeV it gains about three digits ($u overline(u) -> chi_(c 0) thin g$: $2 dot 10^(-8)$ worst instead of $3 dot 10^(-5)$) for 5 to 6 times the time. It needs TIRust d17085a (PR \#56) with the bridge patch v2, not yet in MadGraph.

*Two P-wave bound states* (@twopw): the predicted poles include the dipole-dipole exchange of He, Kniehl and Wang, whose eq. (5) the derivation reproduces (up to a factor 4 and two $J = 1$ misprints there). With TIRust 4f1b06c (TIRust main, now in the pin) the computed poles are as predicted: $e^+ e^- -> chi_(c 0) thin h_c$ to $10^(-10)$, $g g -> chi_(c 0) thin chi_(c 0)$ to $10^(-8)$ up to 20 GeV, also in quadruple precision. With da7902b (TIRust PR \#71) they are too for the other colour assignments and unequal flavours (@twopw16): two octets with a jet to $4 dot 10^(-11)$, a singlet with an octet to $3 dot 10^(-12)$ at 8 GeV, $g g -> chi_(c 1) thin chi_(b 0)$ to $10^(-12)$, whose Born is the tree output's bit for bit. `ONIA_NRQCD_CT` gives the MS-bar counterterm of the exchange. The poles are those of eq. (B.2) of the two-P-wave manuscript (@appb): its table 2 to all seven digits, each of its terms tested; for unequal constituent masses ($B_c$) the virtual has no self-like pole, as eq. (B.2) says; `ONIA_IR_POLES` now has none either (it kept the self term and LDME counterterm of arXiv:2402.19221, off by up to 90% for a $B_c$ octet).

*Every example on TIRust da7902b* with the bridge patch v16 (@v16all): every point the old pin refused is served and stable, and the other results reproduce their records. With $b$ and $t$ excluded from the loops (now the setup of @tab:mg255), the 2.5.5 comparison agrees at every point, to $4 dot 10^(-10)$ in quadruple and $1.4 dot 10^(-8)$ in double precision; with the $10^4$ GeV quarks their counterterm rounding leaves up to $1.5 dot 10^(-5)$ at a 0.9 MeV jet, even in quadruple precision. The stability profiles on da7902b equal those of 5025e12 and of the 80-bit switch on d17085a (@stability-v16), and so do the 80-bit accuracy and cost (@ep).

*MadLoop speed* (@perf): `-O2` builds, tabulated colour contraction and hoisted IEEE checks, bit-identical, faster on every benchmark process. The final campaign, after all the bound-state work (`4ba297a911`, 15 pairs, pinned cores), gives upper 95% bounds of 0.67–0.86. Unit tests and IOTests against the baseline: no failure the baseline does not have, except one sealed TIRust fixture (open items).
open_items: *P-wave in TIRust:* the raised powers at threshold are pinned (`6ba4b53`, @pin6ba). For double precision at high energy, the relation tiers of \#56 (5025e12) with their bridge patch (@stability); the profiles of @stability are not rerun on the pin.

*Binary64 gate of the bridge* (patch 0006, gate $10^(-10)$; MadGraph7\#528): it removes the true double-precision errors of the $J\/psi$, $Upsilon$ tail (@stability). A bridge patch with the gate and the relation tiers together exists; neither is on `onia_loop`'s bridge yet.

*Soft jets:* TIRust refuses the Coulomb triangle and boxes and pentagons with a jet of $p_T$ below about 0.05 GeV (charmonium) to 0.9 GeV ($g g -> eta_b\/Upsilon thin g$); such points are reported unstable. TIRust 08edee3 serves them, and MadLoop's double precision is then silently wrong at the softest: the R2 counterterms of heavy quarks ($M^2$-enhanced; 22% at a 1.5 MeV gluon with the $10^4$ GeV $b$, $t$ of the comparison, $1.7 dot 10^(-4)$ with physical masses), which MadLoop's loop-direction test does not vary. Fixed: bound-state outputs now estimate the rounding of the counterterm interference and rescue such points in quadruple precision (every point right). da7902b serves them too: the $J\/psi$, $Upsilon$ ones are rescued in quadruple precision, the $eta_c$, $eta_b$ ones are within $10^(-5)$ in double precision (@v16all).
*Loop-induced processes* with bound states; the FKS integration on `onia_fks` (its `BinothLHA` can call this virtual).
*80-bit switch:* the bridge patch v2 (inputs as hi + lo words, check pass at the input precision) into MadGraph, then the TIRust pin with it (@ep).

*Two P-wave bound states:* two dotted propagators are pinned (`6ba4b53` serves @tab:ee2p, @tab:gg2p and the singlet with an octet on MadGraph's bridge); still to come, the rank-7 pentagons of raised-power plans (da7902b, TIRust PR \#71) and the bridge patch v16 in MadGraph; a quadruple-precision pass of $g g -> chi_(c 0) thin chi_(c 0)$ takes about 75 minutes, nearly all in MadLoop's binary128 numerator. No one-loop finite part is published to compare with (@twopw).
*MadLoop speed, not yet applied:* rank-limited clearing of the DP updaters' output (it breaks tests that pin full clearing) and the opt-in `-march` builds of the audit.

*Threshold bubbles in double precision:* in the $""^3 S_1^((8))$ channels the gluon that carries the octet has a charm bubble exactly at its threshold, $p^2 = M^2 = 4 m_c^2$. After a boost, $P^2$ in double precision misses it by $10^3$ units (2e-13 at 203 GeV), and the square-root behaviour costs $4 dot 10^(-8)$ that neither loop direction, TIRust's check pass nor a rotation sees (`research/estimate_gap`). Fix: snap such an invariant to $(m_i + m_j)^2$ within the rounding of the momentum components, in TIRust or in MadLoop's bound-state interface.

*Sealed latch fixture:* `ReductionLatchLifecycleTest` compiles stubs from the sealed `tests/input_files/tirust_reduction_latch/stub_check.py` (its SHA-256 is pinned). It renders the stability policy of `loop_matrix_standalone.inc` with the `ninjars_available` switch only, and refuses the bound-state switches there (the counterterm-rounding estimate and the 80-bit rotations), so the test fails on `onia_loop`. The fixture's owner has to admit them.
perf_note: *Where the time goes* (`research/perf_audit.md`, $g g -> t overline(t) g$ with Ninja, before these changes): the loop-numerator updaters (`UPDATE_WL` and the DP-terminal updaters) 45% of the time, the counterterm colour loop 16%, the HELAS routines 8%, the IEEE mode queries of the private updaters 3%. In the audit's full stack (these five changes and C) the colour loop takes 2% and the IEEE queries 0.2%. Not applied: C, the rank-limited clearing of the updaters' output (identical results, but it breaks tests that pin full clearing), and the opt-in `-march` builds.
